---
title: "Specification"
description: "What a studyflow is as a typed graph, what makes one well formed, how its views are derived, what a run does, and how the vocabulary grows."
---

A studyflow is not a diagram with a file beside it, nor a file with a picture beside it. It is one object, and everything the tools do is an operation over that object.

$$S = (N,\ E,\ \mathit{src},\ \mathit{tgt},\ \tau,\ \lambda)$$

$N$ is a finite set of nodes and $E$ a finite set of edges. $\mathit{src}$ and $\mathit{tgt}$ map each edge to its source and target; because they are functions on edges rather than a relation on nodes, two edges may join the same pair, so $S$ is a multigraph. A schema $\Sigma$ fixes the type hierarchy: $\tau$ assigns every node and edge a type from it, and $\lambda$ gives each element the attributes its type allows.

In experimental terms, the nodes are a study's events, tasks, decisions, and data. **Validation** is a set of conditions on $S$, a **projection** is a sub-graph of it, and **execution** is a walk along its control edges.

## Two graphs over one set of nodes

Data elements are nodes like any other, so the data specification and the control flow live in the same object and the *edge type* separates them. The sequence-flow edges induce a control-flow graph $G_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$; the data-association edges induce a data-flow graph $G_{\mathrm{data}}$. The two share every node and no edge: executing $S$ is a walk over the first, and an analysis pipeline is a path through the second.

| Edge | Joins | Carries |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `bpmn:SequenceFlow` | flow node → flow node | control: what happens next, under an optional `conditionExpression` |
| `bpmn:DataInputAssociation`, `bpmn:DataOutputAssociation` | data node ↔ an activity's port | one value in or out of a step, under an optional `transformation` binding |
| `bpmn:MessageFlow` | party ↔ party | an exchange between two parties |

A data association's binding is written `slot = selection`, each half optional: the slot names which argument of the step's call the value fills, the selection names what value arrives. A selection may route a value, never compute one — anything that calculates is a step of its own. Two slots are positions rather than names: `self` binds an unbound method's receiver, `*` appends positionally.

## Types come in layers

Every element is a BPMN 2.0 element first — that is what fixes its shape and how a walk moves through it. Research meaning is layered on top, which is why a generic BPMN tool still reads the file.

```yaml
Survey:
  type: bpmn:Task                       # the process element: shape, and flow behaviour
  name: Post-battery survey
  extensionElements:
    - type: cognitive:Questionnaire     # the research type: meaning, and its own attributes
      instrument: phq-9

Done:
  type: bpmn:EndEvent
  redirectTo: https://example.org/thanks   # a namespaced attribute, straight on the element
```

Some data are drawn — a dataset, a table, a fitted model. Others are the values a run accumulates and later reads: an allocated arm, a running count of failed trials. The second kind is a `bpmn:Property`, declared by a container and never rendered. What unifies them is that the **container fixes the scope**: a value declared on the study lives for one run, one declared on a sub-process for one instance of it. A read resolves outward from the innermost open scope; a write lands on the scope that declares the name.

$G_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ is directed but **not acyclic**. Experimental procedures interrupt, repeat, and exchange turns; an acyclic graph can express those only by pushing the deciding logic outside the graph, where it stops being inspectable. Boundary events, message flows, and choreography state them in the same diagram.

## Well-formedness

| # | Condition | Enforced by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | Every element carries an identifier unique within the file | construction |
| 2 | Both ends of every edge resolve to declared nodes, and a sequence flow's two ends sit in the same container | construction |
| 3 | Every control-flow edge joins flow nodes and every data-flow edge joins a data element to a flow node, so a data node is reachable only through data associations | construction |
| 4 | A node reads or writes a named value only where a containing scope declares it | the executors |
| 5 | The control-flow graph is sound: at least one start event, at least one end event, and every flow node on some path between them | validation, and simulation before a run |
| 6 | A gateway with several outgoing flows carries a rule that picks one — a condition per branch with one marked `default`, or a type that declares how it branches | the executors |
| 7 | Every type is declared by a loaded schema, and every attribute value belongs to the type its schema declares; an attribute no schema declares is kept verbatim and reported, never dropped | validation |
| 8 | The projection of $S$ to BPMN 2.0 is a valid XML document | serialization |

Conditions 1–3 and 8 are structural, and a generic BPMN validator can express most of them. Conditions 4–6 are the domain constraints it cannot: they are what separates a study that is drawable from one that is runnable.

## Projections

Each reading of a studyflow — by a reviewer, a trial manager, an auditor — is a **projection**: given a predicate $p$ over elements, the view is

$$\pi_p(S) = \{\,x \in N \cup E : p(x)\,\}$$

carrying each selected element's attributes exactly as $S$ holds them. A projection **only discards** — it never renames an element, rewrites a type, or computes an attribute the source does not already carry. Because $\pi_p(S) \subseteq S$, a view can be incomplete but cannot be inconsistent with the file it came from.

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![Timeline](assets/img/views/gantt.png){#fig-timeline fig-alt="A Gantt View dialog with rows grouped under Enrolment, Post-allocation, and Close-out, each a labelled bar on a shared horizontal time axis."}

![Checklist](assets/img/views/checklist.png){#fig-checklist fig-alt="A dialog titled Checklist View reading 0 of 52 items complete, with one card per element listing unticked SPIRIT reporting items."}

![Provenance](assets/img/views/provenance.png){#fig-provenance fig-alt="A dialog titled Provenance View listing entries across three runs, each row naming an action, an element, an actor, a tool, and a timestamp."}
:::

| View | Keeps the elements carrying | Answers |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Study** | everything | what happens, in what order, and where the path splits |
| **Timeline** | `onset`, `duration`, or `progress` | when each visit or block falls, and how long it lasts |
| **Checklist** | a checklist documentation entry | which reporting item each step covers, and what is still open |
| **Provenance** | `prov:Activity` entries | which steps ran, when, by whom, and with which seed |
| **Figure** | the elements marked visible | what a reader should see — with the whole of $S$ embedded in the exported image |

That last row is the consequence the rest rests on. A figure exported from a studyflow is not a drawing *about* the study but a subset *of* it: the image carries the complete source, the embedded source rather than the rendering is authoritative, and a reader who wants the omitted part can open it and look. A reporting guideline works the same way — it is a vocabulary, a checklist, and sometimes a flow diagram, which become labels, attributes, and a view, so adherence is a property of the file rather than a spreadsheet kept beside it.

## Execution

A diagram shows every route through a study. A **run** is one traversal: one participant's session, or one pass of a pipeline. It is a walk over $G_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$, deterministic given its initial state — a sequence of configurations $\kappa_n = (s_n, v_n, g_n, \sigma_n)$ binding the study-scoped values, the scopes currently open, the pseudo-random state, and the actor state. Control is a single token occupying one node at a time, so each step is a transition $\kappa_{n+1} = \operatorname{step}(S, \kappa_n, \rho_n)$ with $\rho_n$ the response recorded at step $n$.

| Gateway | Rule |
|:--|:--|
| An exclusive gateway, and `cognitive:EligibilityGateway` | the first outgoing edge whose condition holds, otherwise the edge marked `default` |
| `cognitive:RandomGateway` | a seeded uniform draw over the outgoing edges |
| A parallel gateway | every outgoing edge; the matching join waits for all of them |
| An inclusive gateway | every outgoing edge whose condition holds |
| `agentic:Router` | a label chosen by a model |

A condition is evaluated in the language of the executor reading it, and each executor refuses what it cannot evaluate rather than quietly taking the other branch. A condition naming a value no open scope declares is reported as a defect, not resolved to false. The study's `seed` pins the state a run starts from, so every gateway draw replays — and **nothing beyond them**: participant responses, timing, and randomness inside software a step calls are outside its scope.

The two executors divide by what a step *does*, not by where it sits in the file. Participant-facing steps run in the browser; data-facing steps run in Python; each passes over the other's half. The browser runner picks a screen from what the step *is*, while the Python runner ignores the step's type and calls whatever software it names.

| Element family | Checked before a run | Browser runner | Python runner |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:EndEvent` | consent link shape; completion-code coherence | consent screen; completion screen, code, redirect | reached and recorded, no screen |
| `cognitive:Instruction`, `cognitive:Questionnaire` | empty content or instrument blocks the run | renders; writes the answer into scope | — |
| `cognitive:BehaverseTask` | checked against the assessment build's manifest | runs the assessment in the page | — |
| `cognitive:CognitiveTask`, `cognitive:Rest`, plain `bpmn:Task` | — | generic screen, and a way forward | — |
| Any activity carrying `implementation` | reference grammar; literal arguments must be a mapping | shows the call it names | imports and calls it, binding the drawn data associations |
| `bpmn:SubProcess` | — | descends; opens its own scope | walks one level in; no separate scope |
| `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`, `cognitive:EligibilityGateway` | — | conditions, then `default` | the same rule, in Python |
| `cognitive:RandomGateway` | warns where allocation attributes cannot be honored | seeded uniform draw | treated as exclusive |
| `studyflow:Dataset`, `studyflow:Table`, `studyflow:Timeseries`, `studyflow:Schema`, `studyflow:EventMarker` | — | — | loaded and saved wherever they carry a `uri` |
| `studyflow:Parameters` | reports overridden, undeclared, and unbound names | bound before the walk | — |
| Timers, and multi-instance markers | — | not executed | not executed |

: What each executor does with each family. A blank is a step it passes over. {#tbl-support}

Declaring a type in a schema makes it drawable, inspectable, and storable immediately. It does not make it executable: an element no executor claims is reported twice — before the run, and again as the token reaches it — and stepped past rather than failing the run.

## Provenance

![The document carries both halves: a trail on its root, per-element records beside each element, and — for a pipeline run — a repository whose commits restate the same attributes.](assets/img/diagrams/provenance-model.svg){#fig-provenance-model fig-alt="Flowchart. The studyflow document carries a flat provenance trail on its root element and per-element records in each element's extension elements. The modeler appends to the trail and voids records; the Python runner appends to the trail, stamps records on the archived copy, and commits every checkpoint into a run repository. Each commit restates the trail's attributes as trailers and keeps that checkpoint's step records in its body. No sidecar record file is written." .fig-l}

W3C PROV distinguishes **prospective** provenance, the plan, from **retrospective** provenance, the record of what executed. A studyflow is prospective provenance at deposit and accumulates retrospective provenance as it runs. Both live in the same object, so a deviation report is a *diff between the file's two states* rather than a prose comparison across unrelated documents. Entries are appended oldest first; nothing is overwritten or removed.

| Attribute | Holds | | Action | Records |
|:--|:--|:-:|:--|:--|
| `action` | what happened, in one word | | `created`, `modified` | the file was authored, or edited and exported again |
| `when` | an ISO 8601 timestamp; ties break by position | | `imported` | an artifact was staged in from outside |
| `who` | a name, an email, or an ORCID | | `executed` | the document ran, or one element did |
| `with` | the tool that acted, as `name/version` | | `invalidated` | a marker voiding a named execution record |
| `what` | element ids, or the `when` of the entry referred to | | `reused` | a step was skipped and an earlier record trusted |
| `run`, `seed` | the run's identifier, and its root seed | | | |

The action vocabulary is a recommendation rather than a closed list. A step is skipped only when its record still stands, nothing it reads was re-made this run, and its outputs are still present; invalidation cascades to everything downstream of a re-made output.

## Extending the notation

The domain is never finished, so a vocabulary fixed at publication is wrong within a year, and one that grows by amending the notation breaks every file written against the previous version. Studyflow answers this the way BPMN did: the core covers common designs, and anything further is an extension schema $\Sigma'$ extending the core $\Sigma$. Each new type specializes an existing one and adds its own attributes, so a diagram using it is still well formed and still projects to valid BPMN 2.0.

**Parameterize, do not proliferate.** A verb that is a generic step bound to particular software — *fit a model*, *preprocess one subject* — is a template over an existing type, not a new type; one shipped set declares templates and no types at all.

| Declaring a type gives it | It does not give it |
|:--|:--|
| a place in the palette, a shape, and an icon | a screen or a call in either executor |
| fields in the inspector | pre-flight checks over the values an author types |
| storage and retrieval through every file format | a way for a run to do anything at that step |

The second column is the honest boundary of schema-driven extension, and the reason @tbl-support states element by element what runs today.

| Guarantee | Why it holds |
|:--|:--|
| An extended studyflow is still valid BPMN 2.0 | added types ride inside `extensionElements` and added fields are namespaced attributes — both places the standard reserves |
| A generic BPMN tool reads the file | it consumes the standard elements and ignores namespaces it does not know |
| An attribute no loaded schema declares is preserved | unknown keys are kept verbatim and reported, so a file opened without an optional set and saved again loses nothing |
| The specification outlives the tools | the schemas are maintained apart from the programs that read them, and the file is plain text with a lossless projection to standard XML |

A namespace carries the format version in its own address, and there is no migration mechanism inside a schema: changing a namespace is a breaking change to saved files, made visible rather than absorbed silently.
